source: Recorded from the Go maverick-proxy (internal/proxy) by an instrumented scratch harness: real HTTP servers for the engine, each provider upstream, and the OTLP collector; real proxy handler. Values are byte-exact wire captures.
how_to_replay: Start a mock engine that answers POST /v1/recommend with engine_recommend_response (status, Content-Type application/json, body) and POST /v1/telemetry with 200 {"accepted":1,"dropped":0}. When engine_recommend_response is null the proxy is configured with an unreachable engine URL (http://engine.invalid) and must not call it.

Start one mock upstream per key of provider_scripts. Request N (0-based, per upstream) is answered by provider_scripts[upstream][N]: write headers, write status, then write each body_chunks element followed by a flush. delay_before_headers_ms delays before any header is written. abort_connection_after_chunks aborts the TCP connection after the chunks (no terminating chunk). Requests past the end of a script get 500 {"error":"unscripted request"}.
dead_upstreams_connection_refused lists upstreams whose base URL points at a closed port (http://127.0.0.1:1).
response_header_timeout_ms_override: the capture lowered the 30 s response-header timeout to this value; the production constant is 30000 ms.
proxy_env is the proxy configuration (MAVERICK_API_KEY is mk_live_test in every scenario; telemetry on unless stated). Placeholders <mock ...> are the mock server base URLs (no trailing slash).

inbound_request is sent to the proxy exactly: method, path_and_query, headers in order, body (empty string means no body). The capture client did NOT add Accept-Encoding (compression disabled); Go's client adds Host and Content-Length itself.

expected.recommend_requests / upstream_requests / telemetry_requests are what the mocks received, headers keyed by canonical MIME name. Headers Accept-Encoding: gzip and User-Agent: Go-http-client/1.1 on engine/telemetry/OTLP requests and Accept-Encoding: gzip on upstream requests are added by Go's HTTP client transport, not by proxy code (see reference/engine-reference.md (Part 6) QUIRK list). Host is not recorded.
expected.response.headers excludes Date. Content-Length on streamed responses is absent (chunked).
body_template: <LATENCY_MS> stands for a non-negative integer (milliseconds, truncated) and <UNIX_NANO> for a decimal-string Unix time in nanoseconds; everything else is byte-exact.

otlp_requests_after_forced_flush: after the response the harness called flushLogs() then exportMetrics() and then Server.Close(), which exports metrics once more. That is why metric payloads appear twice (identical cumulative value) and logs once (queue already drained).
Telemetry is asynchronous; the harness waited 300 ms after the response before collecting. Scenarios with an empty telemetry_requests list assert that no telemetry request is ever made.
Scenario ids starting x_ are EXTRA captures of observed Go behavior with no corresponding Go test; they are still parity targets.
